bug_description.original: A use of uninitialized value vulnerability exists in the function ixheaacd_cos_sin_mod, where a local buffer in the complex analysis QMF filter block is not initialized, leading to uninitialized memory access.
bug_description.normalized: The staged libxaac witness drives `ixheaacd_dec_execute()` into SBR decoding and leaves `low_pow_flag == 0`, so `ixheaacd_sbr_dec()` routes the frame into `ixheaacd_cplx_anal_qmffilt()` instead of the LDSBR helper. Vulnerable `ixheaacd_cplx_anal_qmffilt()` allocates `analysis_buffer` on the stack without initialization. Its winadd stage writes only indices `0..63` of that 128-word buffer, but the `!low_pow_flag` path forwards the whole buffer to `ixheaacd_fwd_modulation()`. On this witness the crash stack lands at `ixheaacd_fwd_modulation(...):493`, which proves `qmf_bank->no_channels == 64`; that path reads both halves of `analysis_buffer`, stores values derived from the uninitialized tail into `real_subband`, and then `ixheaacd_cos_sin_mod()` consumes those contaminated values. MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use of uninitialized value in `ixheaac_add32_sat()` at `common/ixheaac_basic_ops32.h:202`. The fix commit resolves the bug by zero-initializing `analysis_buffer` at declaration.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled bytes for the crashing decode pass. This statement wraps the current input chunk into the decoder bit-buffer state that subsequent AAC/SBR parsing uses.
source.value_from: Bytes from the staged witness `/mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_61691/poc`, copied by `Codec::decodeXAACStream()` into libxaac's input buffer and then exposed here through `in_buffer`/`ui_in_bytes`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer sink. `ixheaacd_cos_sin_mod()` passes arithmetic derived from an uninitialized `real_subband` element into this saturated add, and the comparison on `sum` at line 202 is the reported use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: Missing initialization of the stack QMF analysis buffer. The later winadd stage does not overwrite every element before the buffer is consumed, and the patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the declaration to `WORD32 analysis_buffer[4 * NO_ANALYSIS_CHANNELS] = { 0 };`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 used only the saved vulnerable source, patch, and Stage 01 crash artifacts. No fixed-build or cross-tool runtime confirmation was performed here.

The saved artifacts do not preserve which specific header bits among the conditions at `ixheaacd_applysbr():408-418` made `low_pow_flag` stay `0`; the trace anchors that control fact at the first source-visible block where the parsed state is materialized.

Runtime disambiguation stayed disabled for this sample. The trace does not need an extra branch probe for the winadd helper because both `ixheaacd_sbr_qmfanal32_winadd()` and `ixheaacd_sbr_qmfanal32_winadd_eld()` write only `analysis_buffer[0..63]`.

fine_trace.note: The active SBR frame enters `ixheaacd_sbr_dec()` with `low_pow_flag == 0`. The preserved crash stack includes this exact call site, so this forwarding step was executed by the witness.
Because `ldmps_present` is false on this path, `ixheaacd_sbr_dec()` routes the frame into the generic complex-analysis helper `ixheaacd_cplx_anal_qmffilt()` rather than the `_32` LDSBR variant.

Root cause. `analysis_buffer` is a stack array with 128 `WORD32` slots (`4 * NO_ANALYSIS_CHANNELS`, and `NO_ANALYSIS_CHANNELS == 32`) but it starts with indeterminate contents because the vulnerable declaration has no initializer.

The QMF winadd stage only populates the first half of `analysis_buffer`. Both implementations iterate `n = 0; n < 32; n += 2` and assign only `p_out[n]`, `p_out[n + 1]`, `p_out[n + 32]`, and `p_out[n + 33]`, which covers indices `0..63`; `analysis_buffer[64..127]` keep their step-5 stack contents.
Because `low_pow_flag == 0`, the code sends the partially initialized `analysis_buffer` into `ixheaacd_fwd_modulation()` instead of the low-power `ixheaacd_dct3_32()` path.

fine_trace.var: p_time_in1, p_time_in2, temp1, temp2, real_subband, imag_subband, qmf_bank->no_channels
fine_trace.note: On this witness `qmf_bank->no_channels == 64`, which is proven by the saved crash stack landing at line 493. That makes `p_time_in2` start at `&analysis_buffer[127]`, so the loop reads `analysis_buffer[0..63]` through `p_time_in1` and `analysis_buffer[127..64]` through `p_time_in2`. The upper half was never initialized in step 6, and MemorySanitizer records the resulting contaminated store to `real_subband` at line 484.
The first cosine/sine modulation iteration reloads contaminated `real_subband` entries into `re` and `im` and immediately feeds them into `ixheaac_add32_sat()`.
Sink. The saturated-add helper consumes the arithmetic operands derived from step 9, and MemorySanitizer reports the use of uninitialized value at the comparison on `sum` in line 202.

crash_stack.function: Codec::decodeXAACStream(unsigned char*, unsigned int, int*, int*)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSan reports the stack-object origin at the function frame line 596; the patched missing initialization is the declaration of that same object at line 600.

poc.trigger: Running the staged witness with `/bin/arvo run` reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` through `ixheaacd_cos_sin_mod` into `ixheaac_add32_sat`.

format.name: non-ADTS raw libxaac decoder stream
format.contract: This exact 16,439-byte non-ADTS byte stream is the verified trigger. The saved evidence only proves that it drives libxaac into active SBR decoding with `low_pow_flag == 0` and the 64-channel `ixheaacd_fwd_modulation()` path; broader AAC/USAC families or nearby byte patterns are not claimed.
